name: LM2596 adjustable buck converter module (blue board)
description: Steps a higher DC voltage down to an adjustable lower one (default here 5 V), about 2 A continuous, 3 A peak with heatsinking.
notes: The output voltage is set by a trim pot and arrives set to a random value (often the maximum). Power it with nothing connected, measure OUT+ with a multimeter, turn the pot to the target, then connect the load.
IN- and OUT- are the same ground (non-isolated).
No reverse-polarity protection: swapping IN+ and IN- destroys it instantly.
LM2596 chip: 4.5-40 V input, 3 A. Cheap modules use 35 V or lower input capacitors and get hot above about 2 A without a heatsink, so this entry uses 35 V and 2 A.
Needs about 1.5-2 V of headroom: to get 5 V out, feed at least about 7 V.
Efficiency is roughly 75-88 % depending on load and input voltage.
Fakes (counterfeit LM2596) are common and may not reach 3 A.
